title: P-1: inject obligation-source policy via the set manifest
recipe: SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md §5 P-1 (FD-7) — platform work, no recipe doc exists (G-A gap, item 2 of the would-be add-a-set recipe); this plan section is the script

filesToTouch.what: Add one export beside the existing accessors: `export const policy = () => configuredSet?.policy ?? {}`. Deliberately NOT via requireConfiguredSet(): an unconfigured manifest, or a configured set with no policy member, both yield {} (empty-safe defaults per §5 P-1) so L2 units that never configure a set stay green. No other change.

Remove the four literal declarations (SYSTEM_POPULATED line 29, ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE lines 31-34, MAX_ENTRIES_FROM lines 41-43, SYSTEM_ANSWER_KEYS line 70). Import { policy } from '../model/obligations/manifest.js'. Keep the export names SYSTEM_POPULATED and ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE but as lazily-derived membership views resolved per call (nothing computed at module load — the manifest arrives only when configureObligationSet runs): `export const SYSTEM_POPULATED = { has: (name) => (policy().systemPopulated ?? []).includes(name) }` and identically ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE over policy().enforcedAtContinue. Every existing consumer only ever calls .has(), so their import sites compile unchanged. Replace the MAX_ENTRIES_FROM export with `export const maxEntriesCountFieldFor = (collectionName) => (policy().maxEntriesFrom ?? {})[collectionName]` — its lone consumer indexes the object by key, so a plain lazy view cannot serve it without a Proxy; an accessor function is the honest shape (the ONLY consumer-visible signature change in this increment). Replace the internal SYSTEM_ANSWER_KEYS Set with a spread of `policy().systemAnswerKeys ?? []` inside topLevelKeys(). Rewrite the cap comment (currently 'only the declaration lives here') to state the declaration lives on the set manifest's policy.maxEntriesFrom — present-tense, no migration language. After the edit, grep for any obligation-name literal (poApprovedReferenceNumber, countryOfOrigin, commoditySelection, animalIdentifiers, numberOfAnimalsQuantity, referenceNumber) in this file must return nothing.

Swap `import { MAX_ENTRIES_FROM } from '../../bridge/obligation-source.js'` for `import { maxEntriesCountFieldFor }`; line 23 becomes `const countField = maxEntriesCountFieldFor(collectionName)`. Behaviour identical: an undeclared collection yields undefined and the existing null-cap path handles it. Update the file's doc comment (line ~7) so the declaration site reads: declared on the set manifest's policy.maxEntriesFrom, derived through bridge/obligation-source.js.

After the derived `groups` export (line ~235) add today's values verbatim: `export const policy = { systemPopulated: ['poApprovedReferenceNumber'], enforcedAtContinue: ['countryOfOrigin', 'commoditySelection'], maxEntriesFrom: { animalIdentifiers: 'numberOfAnimalsQuantity' }, systemAnswerKeys: ['referenceNumber'] }`. No wiring change anywhere else: routes.js:25/47 and test/setup-obligation-set.js:5/20 already pass this module as a namespace import to configureObligationSet, so the new export flows through automatically.

New unit test (input/output, no mocks) with three describes: (1) a synthetic manifest `{ obligations: [], groups: [], policy: { systemPopulated: ['fieldA'], enforcedAtContinue: ['fieldB'], maxEntriesFrom: { things: 'thingCount' }, systemAnswerKeys: ['customRef'] } }` passed to configureObligationSet changes the derived views — SYSTEM_POPULATED.has('fieldA') true / has('poApprovedReferenceNumber') false, ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE.has('fieldB') true, maxEntriesCountFieldFor('things') === 'thingCount' and ('animalIdentifiers') undefined, unrecognisedAnswerKeys({ customRef: 'x' }) === [] while unrecognisedAnswerKeys({ referenceNumber: 'x' }) flags it; (2) a manifest with NO policy member: every view empty and no throw (empty-safe default); (3) the live-animals manifest derives today's four surfaces (has('poApprovedReferenceNumber'), has('countryOfOrigin'), has('commoditySelection'), maxEntriesCountFieldFor('animalIdentifiers') === 'numberOfAnimalsQuantity', referenceNumber recognised). afterEach restores `configureObligationSet(liveAnimalsObligationSet)` — the vitest setupFile (test/setup-obligation-set.js) configures the singleton once per worker and other tests in this file's worker rely on it.

The count-cap step (~line 298) shows `export const MAX_ENTRIES_FROM = { animalIdentifiers: 'numberOfAnimalsQuantity' }` living in bridge/obligation-source.js. Rewrite the snippet + surrounding sentence: the cap is declared on the set manifest — `policy.maxEntriesFrom = { animalIdentifiers: 'numberOfAnimalsQuantity' }` in sets/live-animals/obligations/index.js — and read through bridge/obligation-source.js `maxEntriesCountFieldFor`; enforcement (cardinality.js collectionCapAt, appendEntryAt rejecting at the cap) unchanged.

Line ~24 links to bridge/obligation-source.js. If the surrounding prose states the cap DECLARATION lives in that file, reword to: declared on the set manifest's policy.maxEntriesFrom and derived through bridge/obligation-source.js (keep the link — the derivation still lives there). If the reference is link-only and already accurate, leave the file unchanged.

notes: Export-shape decision (the one §5 P-1 left to this planner, decided with the grep-verified consumer list in hand): HYBRID of the plan's preferred option (a). SYSTEM_POPULATED and ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE keep their export names as lazily-derived membership views ({ has(name) } objects reading the configured manifest's policy per call) because every consumer — flow/dispatch.js, flow/prerequisites.js, bridge/collection-complete.js, bridge/status/structure/index.js, analysis/flow-reachability/provers.js, analysis/flow-reachability/problems/obligation-problem.js, sets/live-animals/.../flow/entry-guard.js (the legal set→L2 import the plan flags), and flow-reachability.test.js — only ever calls .has(), so eight import sites compile untouched. MAX_ENTRIES_FROM cannot be a lazy view without a Proxy (its single consumer, engine/evaluate/cardinality.js:23, indexes it as a plain object), so that one export becomes the accessor maxEntriesCountFieldFor(collectionName) and only that one consumer changes — explicit-name accessor over Proxy magic, per house style. SYSTEM_ANSWER_KEYS was never exported (module-internal const, verified this session), so it has no external consumers and is replaced by an internal policy read. Consumer set re-verified live against the repo this session and matches §5 P-1's list, with two refinements: bridge/scope.js holds only a comment mention of ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE (stays accurate under shape (a), no edit) and docs/cardinality.md references obligation-source.js by link (conditional prose fix listed). Empty-safe ruling: manifest.policy() returns {} for BOTH an unconfigured manifest and a configured set without a policy member — keeps L2 unit files that never call configureObligationSet green and makes the plant set's future empty policy trivially valid. Rationale for no new Playwright spec: pure behaviour-preserving refactor with zero user-visible change; the regression proof is the existing feature + e2e suites re-run in the ladder. Two-sided sibling check: the plant side is NOT runnable yet (sets/plant-products/ and test:plant-products do not exist until pp-007/pp-010, and pp-005 deliberately has no deps) — the plant-side proof of this seam is pp-007's boot under SERVED_SET=plant-products consuming the FD-7 policy shape { systemPopulated: [], enforcedAtContinue: [], maxEntriesFrom: {}, systemAnswerKeys: ['referenceNumber'] }; the sibling-safety side here is the full live-animals ladder plus the no-test-count-drop check. Exemplars: model/obligations/manifest.js accessor style for the new policy() export; bridge tests that compose a synthetic set (fulfilments.characterisation.test.js pattern) for the new unit test.
